S.source: printed p. 780; entry 'qatidauluk'; illustrates 'qatidauluk'
S.FORM: haya qatidauluk tiktik-in cicu a pa-kan kirpa painan
S.PHON: haja qatidauluk tiktikin θiθu a pakan kirpa painan
S.FORM: haya qatidauluk tiktik-in thithu a pa-kan kirpa painan
S.PHON: haja qatidauluk tiktikin θiθu a pakan kirpa painan
S.TRANSL: Maybe he chopped up the earthworms to feed the ducks

S.source: printed p. 780; entry 'qatitira'; sense 2; illustrates 'kit–qatitira–n'
S.TRANSL: My dog has fleas

S.source: printed p. 780; entry 'qatumu'; illustrates 'qatumu'
S.FORM: haya qatumu a qirqir-an rumfaz mu-shuqish mu-tmaz
S.PHON: haja qatumu a qirqiran rumfað muʃuqiʃ mutmað
S.FORM: haya qatumu a qirqir-an rumfaz mu-shuqish mu-tmaz
S.PHON: haja qatumu a qirqiran rumɸað muʃuqiʃ mutmað
S.TRANSL: The caterpillar which was about to be eaten by the bird crawled back inside

S.source: printed p. 780; entry 'qatumu'; illustrates 'qatumu'
S.TRANSL: The womb where a child stayed

S.source: printed p. 781; entry 'qatumu' (opens on p. 780); illustrates 'qatumu'
S.TRANSL: He wants to return to the womb

S.source: printed p. 781; entry 'qaulh'; sense 2; illustrates 'matug–qaulh'
S.TRANSL: I'll collect water in a bamboo container

S.source: printed p. 781; entry 'qaulh'; sense 3; illustrates 'patug–qaulh'
S.FORM: buhat uka sa sazum, a patug-qaulh yaku
S.PHON: buhat uka sa saðum a patuŋqauɬ jaku
S.FORM: buhat uka sa sazum, a patung-qaulh yaku
S.PHON: buhat uka sa saðum a patuŋqauɬ jaku
S.TRANSL: The field has no water, (so) I'll use the bamboo water pipe

S.source: printed p. 781; entry 'qaulh'; sense 3; illustrates 'patug–qaulh'
S.TRANSL: Pipe the water down from the mountain to fill the lharu (water storage container)

S.source: printed p. 781; entry 'qaur'; illustrates 'qaur'

TRANSL.notes: Source note: as in pinning the head of a snake

S.TRANSL: Hook its head!

S.source: printed p. 781; entry 'qaur'; sense 3; illustrates 'qaur–in'
S.TRANSL: Hook him!

S.source: printed p. 781; entry 'qaur'; sense 5; illustrates 'q–m–aur'
S.FORM: pasay-in cicu ma-kiwar a kawi q-m-aur i-zay a qlhuran cicu a punuq
S.PHON: pasajin θiθu makiwar a kawi qmaur iðaj a qɬuran θiθu a punuq
S.FORM: pasay-in thithu ma-kiwar a kawi q-m-aur i-zay a qlhuran thithu a punuq
S.PHON: pasajin θiθu makiβar a kaβi qmaur iðaj a qɬuran θiθu a punuq
S.TRANSL: He used a curved stick to hook the head of that snake

S.source: printed p. 781; entry 'qauriwa'; illustrates 'qauriwa'
S.TRANSL: Throw out these things!

S.source: printed p. 781; entry 'qauriwa'; illustrates 'qauriwa'
S.TRANSL: Please throw out the garbage

S.source: printed p. 781; entry 'qauriwa'; sense 2; illustrates 'qauriwa–k'

TRANSL.notes: Literal translation: I threw it away, I put it on the side of the road

S.TRANSL: I threw it away on the side of the road

S.source: printed p. 781; entry 'qauriwa'; sense 3; illustrates 'qauriwa–n'
S.FORM: numa sa caw m-zai dai "ma-qarman ya ma-qusu-qusum, ma-puzi-puzi, ma-qulha-qulha", numa sa iza azazak qauriwa-n caycuy p-agqaruz sa sazum, parshian ya malhi-azazak mia-zicu
S.PHON: numa sa θaw mðai dai maqarman ja maqusuqusum mapuðipuði maquɬaquɬa numa sa iða aðaðak qauriwan θajθuj paŋqaruð sa saðum parʃian ja maɬiaðaðak miaðiθu
S.FORM: numa sa thaw m-zai dai "ma-qarman ya ma-qusu-qusum, ma-puzi-puzi, ma-qulha-qulha", numa sa iza azazak qauriwa-n thaythuy p-angqaruz sa sazum, parshian ya malhi-azazak mia-zithu
S.PHON: numa sa θaw mðai dai maqarman ja maqusuqusum mapuðipuði maquɬaquɬa numa sa iða aðaðak qauriβan θajθuj paŋqaruð sa saðum parʃian ja maɬiaðaðak miaðiθu
S.TRANSL: Then the people said "It's bad to have some black, some white, and some red", and they cast the children on the current (because) it is a bad omen to give birth in that way

S.source: printed p. 781; entry 'qawan'; sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'iag–qawan'
S.FORM: iag-qawan a tu kan, kan ihu niza ihu p-in-u-shiqshiq
S.PHON: iaŋqawan a tu kan kan ihu niða ihu pinuʃiqʃiq
S.FORM: iang-qawan a tu kan, kan ihu niza ihu p-in-u-shiqshiq
S.PHON: iaŋqaβan a tu kan kan ihu niða ihu pinuʃiqʃiq
S.TRANSL: Watch out what you eat or you will get diarrhoea

S.source: printed p. 782; entry 'qawan' (opens on p. 781); sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'iag–qawan'
S.FORM: iag-qawan uhu tu mi-qilha, k-anun iza ihu p-in-u-shiqshiq
S.PHON: iaŋqawan uhu tu miqiɬa kanun iða ihu pinuʃiqʃiq
S.FORM: iang-qawan uhu tu mi-qilha, k-anun iza ihu p-in-u-shiqshiq
S.PHON: iaŋqaβan uhu tu miqiɬa kanun iða ihu pinuʃiqʃiq
S.TRANSL: Watch out what you drink (or) you'll get diarrhoea

S.source: printed p. 782; entry 'qawan' (opens on p. 781); sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'iag–qawan'
S.FORM: maqa i-nay a shput mi-lhugqu iag-qawan malhinuna
S.PHON: maqa inaj a ʃput miɬuŋqu iaŋqawan maɬinuna
S.FORM: maqa i-nay a shput mi-lhungqu iang-qawan malhinuna
S.PHON: maqa inaj a ʃput miɬuŋqu iaŋqaβan maɬinuna
S.TRANSL: Because that person is sitting (here) watch what you say

S.source: printed p. 782; entry 'qawan' (opens on p. 781); sense 3; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'ia–qawan'
S.TRANSL: Wait a minute, I don't have time right now

S.source: printed p. 782; entry 'qawan' (opens on p. 781); sense 3; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'ia–qawan'
S.TRANSL: Wait a minute before you go

S.source: printed p. 782; entry 'qawan' (opens on p. 781); sense 4; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'mia–qawan'
S.FORM: nak a binanau'az mia-qawan malhus shashanu, numa antu mi-lhilhi pit'ia, numa fanuz-ik shu-azaz-ik pinuqrum
S.PHON: nak a binanauʔað miaqawan maɬus ʃaʃanu numa antu miɬiɬi pitʔia numa fanuðik ʃuaðaðik pinuqrum
S.FORM: nak a binanau'az mia-qawan malhus shashanu, numa antu mi-lhilhi pit'ia, numa fanuz-ik shu-azaz-ik pinuqrum
S.PHON: nak a binanauʔað miaqaβan maɬus ʃaʃanu numa antu miɬiɬi pitʔia numa ɸanuðik ʃuaðaðik pinuqrum
S.TRANSL: My wife slept late this morning and didn't get up to cook, so I woke (her) up by pulling off her blanket

S.source: printed p. 782; entry 'qawan' (opens on p. 781); sense 4; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'mia–qawan'
S.TRANSL: It has been raining continuously without a break

S.source: printed p. 782; entry 'qawan' (opens on p. 781); sense 4; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'mia–qawan'
S.FORM: ya mia-qawan makin-damu antu a m-acay, ya niza tu makin-damu niza tu a mia-ramaz
S.PHON: ja miaqawan makindamu antu a maθaj ja niða tu makindamu niða tu a miaramað
S.FORM: ya mia-qawan makin-damu antu a m-athay, ya niza tu makin-damu niza tu a mia-ramaz
S.PHON: ja miaqaβan makindamu antu a maθaj ja niða tu makindamu niða tu a miaramað
S.TRANSL: If a person still can groan he isn't dead yet (but) if he can't groan one must take precautions

S.source: printed p. 782; entry 'qaz'; illustrates 'qaz'

TRANSL.notes: Source note: e.g. telling someone to smell a blossom

S.TRANSL: Try it, test it

S.source: printed p. 782; entry 'qaz'; illustrates 'qaz'
S.FORM: qaz uan ihu cicu mig-qulha na shaqish, maqa m-in-i-qilha, maqa t-in-ilhaz-in, maqa min-iaw
S.PHON: qað uan ihu θiθu miŋquɬa na ʃaqiʃ maqa miniqiɬa maqa tiniɬaðin maqa miniaw
S.FORM: qaz uan ihu thithu ming-qulha na shaqish, maqa m-in-i-qilha, maqa t-in-ilhaz-in, maqa min-iaw
S.PHON: qað uan ihu θiθu miŋquɬa na ʃaqiʃ maqa miniqiɬa maqa tiniɬaðin maqa miniaw
S.TRANSL: Look at him: his face is getting red because he drank, because he was in the sun, because he is embarrassed

S.source: printed p. 782; entry 'qaz'; illustrates 'qaz'
S.FORM: qaz uan tug-qa-qaur shkish k-m-ay cakcak lhuzush
S.PHON: qað uan tuŋqaqaur ʃkiʃ kmaj θakθak ɬuðuʃ
S.FORM: qaz uan tung-qa-qaur shkish k-m-ay thakthak lhuzush
S.PHON: qað uan tuŋqaqaur ʃkiʃ kmaj θakθak ɬuðuʃ
S.TRANSL: Please make the bamboo into a hook to down some plums

S.source: printed p. 782; entry 'qaz'; sense 2; illustrates 'qaz–i'
S.TRANSL: Try to see if you can succeed (in doing something)

S.source: printed p. 782; entry 'qaz'; sense 2; illustrates 'qaz–i'
S.FORM: qaz-i uan ya tima sa i-zuy a shput
S.PHON: qaði uan ja tima sa iðuj a ʃput
S.FORM: qaz-i uan ya tima sa i-zuy a shput
S.PHON: qaði uan ja tima sa iðuj a ʃput
S.TRANSL: Please see who that person is

S.source: printed p. 782; entry 'qaz'; sense 2; illustrates 'qaz–i'
S.FORM: numa a i-utu malhus qaz-i a numa wa aki, numa tu ma-humhum iza i-utu malhus matiashaq
S.PHON: numa a iutu maɬus qaði a numa wa aki numa tu mahumhum iða iutu maɬus matiaʃaq
S.FORM: numa a i-utu malhus qaz-i a numa wa aki, numa tu ma-humhum iza i-utu malhus matiashaq
S.PHON: numa a iutu maɬus qaði a numa βa aki numa tu mahumhum iða iutu maɬus matiaʃaq
S.TRANSL: Then they stayed there sleeping to see if there was a god (and) then when it was dark they slept there and dreamt

S.source: printed p. 782; entry 'qaz'; sense 2; illustrates 'qaz–i'
S.FORM: qaz-i ya mu-nay m-ihu a binanau'az
S.PHON: qaði ja munaj mihu a binanauʔað
S.FORM: qaz-i ya mu-nay m-ihu a binanau'az
S.PHON: qaði ja munaj mihu a binanauʔað
S.TRANSL: Try to get your wife to come

S.source: printed p. 782; entry 'qaz'; sense 2; illustrates 'qaz–i'
S.FORM: qaz-i uan haya binanau'az ya ma-qitan
S.PHON: qaði uan haja binanauʔað ja maqitan
S.FORM: qaz-i uan haya binanau'az ya ma-qitan
S.PHON: qaði uan haja binanauʔað ja maqitan
S.TRANSL: See if that woman is pretty

S.source: printed p. 782; entry 'qaz'; sense 2; illustrates 'qaz–i'
S.FORM: qaz-i ya alha kaiza ya m-usha?
S.PHON: qaði ja aɬa kaiða ja muʃa
S.FORM: qaz-i ya alha kaiza ya m-usha?
S.PHON: qaði ja aɬa kaiða ja muʃa
S.TRANSL: When will you go?

S.source: printed p. 782; entry 'qaz'; sense 2; illustrates 'qaz–i'

TRANSL.notes: Source note: as when hearing a noise outside

S.TRANSL: What is that?

S.source: printed p. 783; entry 'qaz' (opens on p. 782); sense 2; illustrates 'qaz–i'
S.FORM: haya tuali shupilh uan ihu qaz-i a ma-lunduz
S.PHON: haja tuali ʃupiɬ uan ihu qaði a malunduð
S.FORM: haya tuali shupilh uan ihu qaz-i a ma-lunduz
S.PHON: haja tuali ʃupiɬ uan ihu qaði a malunduð
S.TRANSL: Please count that money to see if it is right

S.source: printed p. 783; entry 'qazaiku'; illustrates 'qazaiku'
S.TRANSL: I thought you were writing

S.source: printed p. 783; entry 'qazaiku'; illustrates 'qazaiku'
S.FORM: qazaiku mia-zicu m-zai "runrun-in", ani zai-n "qayu" ya mia-zicu
S.PHON: qaðaiku miaðiθu mðai runrunin ani ðain qaju ja miaðiθu
S.FORM: qazaiku mia-zithu m-zai "runrun-in", ani zai-n "qayu" ya mia-zithu
S.PHON: qaðaiku miaðiθu mðai runrunin ani ðain qaju ja miaðiθu
S.TRANSL: I thought you said "runrun-in", but that wasn't it-you said "qayu", didn't you?

S.source: printed p. 783; entry 'qazaiku'; illustrates 'qazaiku'
S.FORM: qazaiku ihu tilha maku-na-nay, cuini uan ihu shau-na-na-nay
S.PHON: qaðaiku ihu tiɬa makunanaj θuini uan ihu ʃaunananaj
S.FORM: qazaiku ihu tilha maku-na-nay, thuini uan ihu shau-na-na-nay
S.PHON: qaðaiku ihu tiɬa makunanaj θuini uan ihu ʃaunananaj
S.TRANSL: I thought you came yesterday, but you came today

S.source: printed p. 783; entry 'qazaiku'; illustrates 'qazaiku'
S.FORM: nak a ina qazaiku nak a ama ma-fazaq ma-qa-quyash
S.PHON: nak a ina qaðaiku nak a ama mafaðaq maqaqujaʃ
S.FORM: nak a ina qazaiku nak a ama ma-fazaq ma-qa-quyash
S.PHON: nak a ina qaðaiku nak a ama maɸaðaq maqaqujaʃ
S.TRANSL: My mother thinks my father really knows how to sing

S.source: printed p. 783; entry 'qazaiku'; illustrates 'qazaiku'
S.TRANSL: I think you are good at catching fish

S.source: printed p. 783; entry 'qazi–qazi'; illustrates 'qazi–qazi'
S.FORM: qazi-qazi uan nak a azazak ya ikahi
S.PHON: qaðiqaði uan nak a aðaðak ja ikahi
S.FORM: qazi-qazi uan nak a azazak ya ikahi
S.PHON: qaðiqaði uan nak a aðaðak ja ikahi
S.TRANSL: Please look after my children

S.source: printed p. 783; entry 'qazi–qazi'; sense 2; illustrates 'q–m–azi–qazi'
S.FORM: haya wa aniamin azaz yaku sa q-m-azi-qazi
S.PHON: haja wa aniamin aðað jaku sa qmaðiqaði
S.FORM: haya wa aniamin azaz yaku sa q-m-azi-qazi
S.PHON: haja βa aniamin aðað jaku sa qmaðiqaði
S.TRANSL: I'll look after all those things

S.source: printed p. 783; entry 'qazi–qazi'; sense 2; illustrates 'q–m–azi–qazi'
S.TRANSL: She looked after my children

S.source: printed p. 783; entry 'qazpu'; sense 2; illustrates 'uka sa qazpu'
S.FORM: haya wa caw uka sa qazpu
S.PHON: haja wa θaw uka sa qaðpu
S.FORM: haya wa thaw uka sa qazpu
S.PHON: haja βa θaw uka sa qaðpu

TRANSL.notes: Literal translation: That man has no gall

S.TRANSL: That man is a coward

S.source: printed p. 783; entry 'qazus'; sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'mu–qazus'
S.FORM: shu-na-faw sa ruza qucquc-i sa ruza a maqa antu a mu-qazus
S.PHON: ʃunafaw sa ruða quθquθi sa ruða a maqa antu a muqaðus
S.FORM: shu-na-faw sa ruza quthquth-i sa ruza a maqa antu a mu-qazus
S.PHON: ʃunaɸaw sa ruða quθquθi sa ruða a maqa antu a muqaðus
S.TRANSL: Pull the boat up (to shore) and tie it so that it won't drift away

S.source: printed p. 783; entry 'qazus'; sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'mu–qazus'
S.FORM: dadú a binanau'az azazak i sa ruza m-untal ruza mu-qazus, ba! pan-na-tusi kay p-acay-in Rawaraway
S.PHON: dadu a binanauʔað aðaðak i sa ruða muntal ruða muqaðus ba pannatusi kaj paθajin rawarawaj
S.FORM: dadu a binanau'az azazak i sa ruza m-untal ruza mu-qazus, ba! pan-na-tusi kay p-athay-in Rawaraway
S.PHON: dadu a binanauʔað aðaðak i sa ruða muntal ruða muqaðus ba pannatusi kaj paθajin raβaraβaj
S.TRANSL: The chief's daughter in the boat drifted away with the boat (and) my god! over there she was killed by strangers

S.source: printed p. 783; entry 'qazus'; sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'mu–qazus'
S.FORM: haya kawi mu-qazus shan'awan i-saháy tug-kiwar
S.PHON: haja kawi muqaðus ʃanʔawan isahaj tuŋkiwar
S.FORM: haya kawi mu-qazus shan'awan i-sahay tung-kiwar
S.PHON: haja kaβi muqaðus ʃanʔaβan isahaj tuŋkiβar
S.TRANSL: This log was drifting and got stuck there when it was turning around a bend (in the river)

S.source: printed p. 783; entry 'qazus'; sense 4; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'pu–qazus–in'; reading 1 of 2 of "(sa) nak a ruza a'a ma–qitan pu–qazus–in ihu"
S.FORM: nak a ruza a'a ma-qitan pu-qazus-in ihu
S.PHON: nak a ruða aʔa maqitan puqaðusin ihu
S.FORM: nak a ruza a'a ma-qitan pu-qazus-in ihu
S.PHON: nak a ruða aʔa maqitan puqaðusin ihu
S.TRANSL: Why did you set my boat adrift for no good reason?

S.source: printed p. 783; entry 'qazus'; sense 4; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'pu–qazus–in'; reading 2 of 2 of "(sa) nak a ruza a'a ma–qitan pu–qazus–in ihu"
S.FORM: sa nak a ruza a'a ma-qitan pu-qazus-in ihu
S.PHON: sa nak a ruða aʔa maqitan puqaðusin ihu
S.FORM: sa nak a ruza a'a ma-qitan pu-qazus-in ihu
S.PHON: sa nak a ruða aʔa maqitan puqaðusin ihu
S.TRANSL: Why did you set my boat adrift for no good reason?

S.source: printed p. 783; entry 'qazus'; sense 5; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'q–in–azus'
S.TRANSL: My boat has drifted away

S.source: printed p. 784; entry 'qbit'; illustrates 'qbit'
S.TRANSL: one pile, one heap (of something unspecified)

S.source: printed p. 784; entry 'qbit'; illustrates 'qbit'
S.TRANSL: a bundle of firewood

S.source: printed p. 784; entry 'qbit'; illustrates 'qbit'
S.TRANSL: two bundles of firewood

S.source: printed p. 784; entry 'qbit'; illustrates 'qbit'
S.TRANSL: That portion is bigger

S.source: printed p. 784; entry 'qbit'; sense 3; illustrates 'mia–qbit'

TRANSL.notes: Source note: into different groups, households, etc.

S.TRANSL: We are separated

S.source: printed p. 784; entry 'qbit'; sense 3; illustrates 'mia–qbit'
S.TRANSL: My house is in a separate location over there on the other side

S.source: printed p. 784; entry 'qbit'; sense 3; illustrates 'mia–qbit mia–qbit'
S.FORM: m-ihu sa iza aniamin mia-qbit, numa sa i-zay nak a mia-qbit
S.PHON: mihu sa iða aniamin miaqbit numa sa iðaj nak a miaqbit
S.FORM: m-ihu sa iza aniamin mia-qbit, numa sa i-zay nak a mia-qbit
S.PHON: mihu sa iða aniamin miaqbit numa sa iðaj nak a miaqbit

TRANSL.notes: Source note: as of food, etc.

S.TRANSL: This is your share, and this is mine

S.source: printed p. 784; entry 'qbit'; sense 3; illustrates 'mia–qbit'
S.TRANSL: I belong to the other group

S.source: printed p. 784; entry 'qbit'; sense 4; illustrates 'pia–qbit'
S.TRANSL: Divide up those sweet potatoes and put them here

S.source: printed p. 784; entry 'qca'; sense 3; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'kan qca–k'
S.FORM: i-zay a kukulay a kan qca-k
S.PHON: iðaj a kukulaj a kan qθak
S.FORM: i-zay a kukulay a kan qtha-k
S.PHON: iðaj a kukulaj a kan qθak
S.TRANSL: I will step on that bug

S.source: printed p. 784; entry 'qca'; sense 6; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'k–m–an qca'
S.FORM: cicu i-say bukhaz mi-lhugqu, k-m-an qca sa kukulay
S.PHON: θiθu isaj bukhað miɬuŋqu kman qθa sa kukulaj
S.FORM: thithu i-say bukhaz mi-lhungqu, k-m-an qtha sa kukulay
S.PHON: θiθu isaj bukhað miɬuŋqu kman qθa sa kukulaj
S.TRANSL: He sat on the floor (and) crushed a bug

S.source: printed p. 784; entry 'qca'; sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'kashi–qca–n'
S.FORM: nak a taun maqa sasaz iza a kashi-qca-n
S.PHON: nak a taun maqa sasað iða a kaʃiqθan
S.FORM: nak a taun maqa sasaz iza a kashi-qtha-n
S.PHON: nak a taun maqa sasað iða a kaʃiqθan
S.TRANSL: Because my house is old it is going to be renovated

S.source: printed p. 784; entry 'qca'; sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'mu–qca'
S.TRANSL: Will you fight again?

S.source: printed p. 784; entry 'qca'; sense 3; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'kashug–qca–qca'
